title: Bandwidth-aware prioritized sync and store-and-forward data movement between edge applications and the NGC2/TAK data layer (policy-driven 'what leaves first, at what fidelity' and COP-edit reconciliation on reconnect)

scores.rationale: Real but partially solved pain: DDIL links of 1 Mbps-1 kbps are the stated operating regime (DARPA FLUID, darpa.mil, 2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH) and the hub-and-spoke NGC2 redesign was driven by bandwidth/latency problems (Federal News Network, 2025-10, FACT/MEDIUM); but the store-and-forward/re-sync primitive already works at division scale (Ivy Mass, army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH), and the residual pain (manual deconfliction of COP objects, arrival-order replication) is an INFERENCE with LOW confidence - no public government document quantifies it. Public evidence insufficient to rate above 3.

Partition and reconnect events happen in every DDIL exercise and would happen continuously in contested operations; Ivy Mass deliberately injected EMI, cyber and comms loss (army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH), and FLUID's whole premise is chronic rather than episodic link scarcity (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Not a 5 because in garrison and benign-network training the pain is largely absent.

Money exists nearby but none is addressed to this layer: NGC2 ~$3.3B identified through FY2026 with no life-cycle estimate and a 50% FY26 NDAA obligation cap (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH); AFLCMC's Ditto contract is $28M ceiling with ~$5.3M obligated (GlobalSecurity, 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH) - ceiling is not revenue; DARPA FLUID funds research performers. No RFI, SBIR topic or budget line names a standalone prioritization/reconciliation policy layer (Public evidence insufficient).

Score of 1 explained: every route to the user passes through an incumbent-owned gate. The Army formally assigned the NGC2 common data layer baseline to Anduril with Palantir Foundry and Raft (army.mil, 2026-06-22, FACT/HIGH); the Air Force sole-sourced Ditto (2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH); TAK Product Center owns the Mission API. The card's own entry path is 'subcontractor to a prime or TAK plugin'. SBIR - the only open competitive lane for this class of software - is gated by the >50% U.S.-person ownership test (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH) that excludes the Indonesian founder's equity, and SBIR authority lapsed Sep 30, 2025 with reauthorization in progress in 2026 (DefenseScoop, 2026-04-29, FACT/MEDIUM). No independent PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> VEHICLE chain exists for a standalone vendor.

A mission-priority scheduler, fidelity-degradation pipeline and auditable merge-rule engine over CoT/TAK objects are well-understood distributed-systems work (priority queues, CRDT/DTN patterns per RFC 9171, netem link shaping); ATAK-CIV and TAK Server docs are public (github.com/deptofdefense/AndroidTacticalAssaultKit-CIV; docs.opentakserver.io, FACT/MEDIUM). Not a 5 because the hard part - correct merge semantics for C2 objects edited on both sides of a partition without silent data loss - is subtle and unvalidated without real exercise data.

The card's capital table (HYPOTHESIS, no direct public data) puts a proof of concept at $150k-$300k, so $250k reaches a lab demo; but a credible military demo is $1M-$2.5M and requires an integrator sprint slot, and the PoC alone proves nothing to buyers who already have Ditto and Lattice Mesh in production. Capital reaches the first rung of a ladder whose upper rungs are not funded.

A side-by-side shaped-link demo (naive TAK replication vs policy-driven) on commercial laptops, SBCs and throttled Starlink/mesh radios is realistic in 4-6 months (card MVP section, HYPOTHESIS/MEDIUM). A demo the actual buyer treats as credible (inside an Ivy Sting-type sprint via a prime, or with TAK-GOV) depends on a third party's calendar and is 12-24 months out at best.

CoT schemas, ATAK-CIV source and TAK Server Mission API docs are public (FACT/HIGH-MEDIUM); representative message mixes and link traces can be synthesized or self-measured on commercial mesh radios and Starlink. The data that would make the policy library valuable - real exercise partition events, message mixes per mission phase and reconciliation actions - is CUI and only reachable inside an NGC2 team or via a C5ISR Center CRADA (card data_requirement; E07-F30 on CUI access, FACT/MEDIUM).

The MVP is unclassified, EAR-territory software on open TAK-CIV and commercial radios (card regulatory_burden 'medium'; E07-F32 on encryption being a notification step, FACT/MEDIUM). Beyond MVP: TAK-GOV/MIL distribution control, CUI exercise data, ATO inheritance inside a prime's environment, possibly ITAR-adjacent radio technical data, and deemed-export/FOCI questions for the Indonesian founder (E07-F3, E07-F7, E07-F30, FACT). These are constraints requiring export-control and immigration counsel, not a legal determination here.

Everything needed for the first 6-12 months is open: ATAK-CIV, OpenTAKServer/TAK Server docs, Linux tc/netem, commercial hardware, synthetic data; classification dependence is 'eventually' (card), i.e., only when tuning against real exercise data or deploying inside NGC2. Not a 5 because the commercially decisive validation step (real partition data, TAK-GOV) is controlled or CUI.

Score of 1 explained: the field is occupied by well-capitalized, contracted incumbents at every layer - Ditto (~$136M raised incl. $82M Mar 2025, TechCrunch 2025-03-12; AFLCMC $28M-ceiling sole-source; DIU COD success memo; ATAK Edge Sync plugin), Anduril Lattice Mesh (CDAO 3-year production agreement Dec 2024, Breaking Defense; NGC2 data-layer lead Jun 2026), Palantir Foundry edge, Raft, government-owned TAK Server Mission API, DARPA FLUID performers generating government-funded IP through 2028, transport vendors (Persistent, Silvus, goTenna) with their own QoS, and commodity local-first stacks (PowerSync, ElectricSQL, Couchbase Lite) that lower primes' build cost. All FACT/HIGH-MEDIUM from the card's sources.

Score of 1 explained: the incumbents own the sync loop, the link telemetry and the APIs; the card's own analysis (INFERENCE, HIGH) is that a priority scheduler plus merge-rule engine is 'weeks-to-months of work' for Anduril/Palantir, Ditto or TAK Product Center, and each has a lock-in incentive to build it in-house. Anduril opened the Lattice Mesh SDK to third parties under CDAO's ecosystem model (Breaking Defense, 2024-12, FACT/MEDIUM), which invites plugins on its terms rather than exposing it to displacement. No GAO/IG or after-action finding evidences operator dissatisfaction with current re-sync behavior (Public evidence insufficient).

Technically the hooks exist (TAK Server Mission API/Data Sync, Lattice SDK gRPC/REST opened to third parties, Ditto SDK), but the startup controls none of them (card integration_requirement, FACT/MEDIUM); deployment inside NGC2 hubs requires the prime's Kubernetes environment and ATO inheritance; link telemetry from MANET/pLEO radios needs vendor API access. Integration is feasible only with the interface owner's cooperation, which is exactly what a competing policy layer would not receive.

Score of 1 explained: the only proposed proprietary assets are a policy library, measured link models and per-object merge rules - all of which the engine owners can observe and replicate from the same exercise data they already hold; a sidecar accrues no network effects, no accreditation moat and no data exclusivity (card defensibility, INFERENCE/HIGH). The DDIL harness variant has impartiality as its value, which is a positioning, not a moat.

Generic bandwidth-aware sync has commercial analogues (aviation, maritime, retail, IoT, disaster-response TAK-CIV users such as FEMA/CBP/wildland fire), but that generic demand is already served by Ditto's commercial business and open-source local-first stacks; the differentiating pieces (mission-phase policy, C2-object merge semantics) are military-specific with little commercial pull (card dual_use 'medium'; scored below the card's label because the differentiated part is the non-dual-use part, INFERENCE/MEDIUM).

Adjacent moves exist on paper - Air Force expeditionary comms (ACC AMIC RFI asks for application-level QoS inside a comms kit, sam.gov, 2026-01, FACT/MEDIUM), Navy COD, allied TAK users (NATO, UK Project Asgard, German D-LBO) - but each has its own incumbents (blackned, Systematic, Thales, Anduril UK) and a plugin/subcontractor position does not compound into a platform; the card's allied_extension concludes it is a niche service business.

If adopted inside a prime's stack the software would be sustained and re-licensed annually through the prime's OTA/task orders, and TAK plugins can be re-bought by many units; but the buyer relationship is intermediated, the incumbent can absorb the feature at any renewal, and no independent recurring line exists (INFERENCE/MEDIUM).

One strong engineer plausibly covers the distributed-systems/CRDT core, and the business founder can run SBIR/xTech and BD; but three fatal-if-absent roles are missing (TAK/NGC2 integration engineer, former S6/G6 or fires-cell operator to define credible mission-phase policies, export/FOCI counsel), the Indonesian founder cannot count toward the SBIR >50% U.S.-person majority or be technical lead on an AFWERX award without restructuring (E07-F3, E07-F7, FACT/HIGH), the German founder's equity only counts post-green-card, and the team has no prime relationships. Fit is real on the technical wedge and weak on every access dimension; requires counsel, not a legal judgment here.

market.summary: Not unsolved (Ivy Mass re-sync demonstrated May 2026); every interface is owned by a contracted incumbent (Ditto AFLCMC $28M ceiling; Anduril/Palantir/Raft NGC2 data-layer baseline Jun 2026; TAK Mission API); no budget line for 'prioritization policy'; government funds the residual as DARPA FLUID research, not a product buy; NGC2 itself is under a 50% obligation cap with no cost estimate (GAO-26-108019). Outcome is plugin shop or small acqui-hire. Narrower survivable form: a DDIL sync-behavior test harness.

competition.summary: Three incumbent engines (Ditto, Lattice Mesh/Foundry, TAK Server) already ship the primitive at the target echelon and DDIL regime; two services have formally picked owners for this interface (Army NGC2 baseline, AFLCMC sole-source); the residual policy/merge layer is weeks-to-months of work for teams that own the sync loop and have lock-in incentives; the acquisition environment is tightening around primes, not opening. Narrower survivable form: vendor-agnostic DDIL test/certification tooling.

feasibility.summary: MVP is unclassified and cheap, but $250k buys only a PoC that proves nothing to buyers already running Ditto/Lattice; credible demo ($1-2.5M) and production ($5-10M, subcontractor-only) require a prime or PEO C3N sponsor on a 3-5 year chain with no funded step; SBIR ownership (13 CFR 121.702) and AFWERX foreign-national limits (E07-F3/F7) block the Indonesian founder from the qualifying majority and technical lead; missing operator and integration expertise. Narrower survivable form: netem/tc-based DDIL harness sold to program offices and primes, with a U.S.-person-compliant structure.

verdict_rationale: All three skeptics refute at strength 5 and this analyst agrees; no evidence in the card, the E01/E02 findings or the E07 regulatory sweep contradicts them. The decisive reason is structural, not technical: there is no identifiable independent path PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> CONTRACT VEHICLE for a standalone 'prioritization and reconciliation policy layer'. The requirement owner (Army Futures Command/Network CFT, T2COM) and program office (PEO C3N) have already routed the data-layer function to a prime-owned baseline (Anduril lead with Palantir Foundry and Raft, army.mil 2026-06-22, FACT/HIGH); the Air Force routed its equivalent to Ditto by sole-source (GlobalSecurity 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH); the government-owned TAK baseline provides the reconnect re-sync primitive for free (OpenTAKServer docs, FACT/MEDIUM); and the residual application-aware load-reduction problem is being funded as DARPA FLUID research (darpa.mil 2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH), not solicited as a product. The store-and-forward/re-sync capability the founders would headline was demonstrated at division scale in Ivy Mass (army.mil 2026-06, FACT/HIGH). What remains is a feature that four interface owners can add in weeks-to-months (INFERENCE, HIGH), leaving a two-person team with a $250k PoC and no funded next step, no unclaimed acquisition lane, an SBIR ownership problem (13 CFR 121.702, FACT/HIGH), and a best case of TAK-plugin subcontracting or a small acqui-hire. Major penalty applied for the missing procurement chain. The user-pain is real (criteria 1-2 score 3-4) but the market-side criteria for budget, access, competition, incumbent vulnerability and moat all score 1-2, producing market attractiveness 2.1; founder fit of 3.0 reflects only that the unclassified MVP is cheap and open, not that the founders can reach a buyer.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not enough to lift G17 to borderline, but worth logging as a separate candidate: a vendor-agnostic DDIL network-emulation and sync-behavior test harness (Linux tc/netem link profiles from 1 Mbps to 1 kbps, scripted partition/reconnect storms across ~10 simulated ATAK-CIV/TAK Server nodes, scoring time-to-arrival of priority CoT objects, duplicate/conflicting objects after reconnect, link saturation on reconnect, with a reconcile-log audit). Its only evidenced demand signal is the Army SBIR topic 'Generative AI Enabled Tactical Network' asking for a DDIL modeling environment (armysbir.army.mil, 2025, FACT/HIGH), which is a measurement/modeling ask rather than a certification-harness buy; plausible buyers (PEO C3N, DEVCOM C5ISR Center, prime T&E organizations, DOT&E) are HYPOTHESIS with LOW confidence and no dedicated budget line. It is a tooling/services business, SBIR-gated (so it needs a >50% U.S.-person cap table and a U.S.-person technical lead per E07-F3/F7, counsel required), and is not venture-scale. It should be scored as its own gap with its own evidence card rather than treated as a rescue of G17.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders insisted on spending $250k here, the only defensible first build is not the policy layer but the measuring instrument: an open, reproducible DDIL sync test bench - ATAK-CIV clients and TAK Server (later a Ditto SDK adapter, and a Lattice SDK adapter if access is granted) on ~10 commercial SBCs/laptops behind Linux tc/netem profiles spanning 1 Mbps to 1 kbps with scripted 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms, producing a scored report of what arrived first, at what fidelity, how many duplicate or conflicting COP objects appeared after reconnect, and whether the link saturated. They would show it to DEVCOM C5ISR Center tactical-network S&T leads, the TAK Product Center, a Team Anduril or Team Lockheed data-layer lead, and an AFWERX/AFLCMC BES program manager who already funds Ditto; the demonstration would prove, with numbers no vendor marketing provides, whether the fielded engines deliver mission-priority behavior under thin links and where reconciliation fails. A program office would care because GAO-26-108019 (2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH) has just criticized NGC2 for missing cost and schedule evidence and Congress has capped obligations pending a report, so objective before/after metrics for the data layer have near-term bureaucratic value, and primes would care because such evidence supports their own acceptance testing. An incumbent cannot trivially crush the harness because its value is impartiality - Anduril or Ditto scoring their own stack is not evidence a program office can use - though nothing stops the government from building it in-house or a prime from ignoring it. The milestone that would justify the next $2-5M is a funded, named instrument: a SBIR Phase II or PEO C3N/C5ISR Center task order that adopts the harness as an acceptance-test capability, plus a signed integrator letter agreeing to consume a policy API produced from its findings - which is the only credible way the original G17 policy-layer idea ever re-enters. Absent that, the honest answer is that G17 fails because the money and the interface are already assigned: the store-and-forward primitive works (Ivy Mass, May 2026), the residual policy/merge layer is a modest extension for four interface owners, DARPA is funding the research path through FLUID, no buyer has asked for a standalone policy product, and SBIR ownership rules complicate the one open lane for this team; the founders should carry the harness forward as a separate small candidate and put their venture-scale ambitions elsewhere.
bear_case_summary: Feature, not product. The re-sync primitive is fielded inside the prime's NGC2 stack (Ivy Mass, army.mil, 2026-06, FACT/HIGH), the interfaces are owned by Anduril/Palantir/Raft (NGC2 baseline, 2026-06-22, FACT/HIGH), Ditto (AFLCMC sole-source $28M ceiling, ~$5.3M obligated, 2025-07-11, FACT/HIGH) and the government-owned TAK Server Mission API; no RFI, SBIR topic or budget line asks for a standalone prioritization/reconciliation policy layer (Public evidence insufficient); DARPA FLUID funds the residual problem as research (2025-03-28, FACT/HIGH); NGC2 has no life-cycle cost estimate and a 50% obligation cap (GAO-26-108019, 2026-08-20, FACT/HIGH); incumbents can add the layer in weeks-to-months (INFERENCE, HIGH); SBIR ownership (13 CFR 121.702) and AFWERX foreign-national rules exclude the Indonesian founder from the qualifying majority and technical lead (E07-F3/F7, FACT/HIGH); $250k buys a PoC that proves nothing to buyers already running Ditto and Lattice. Best case is a TAK plugin subcontract or a small acqui-hire.
bull_case_summary: The pain is real and recurring: DDIL is the stated regime (DARPA FLUID 1 Mbps-1 kbps), NGC2 was re-architected hub-and-spoke because of bandwidth/latency (Federal News Network, 2025-10, FACT/MEDIUM), ACC's AMIC RFI asks for application-level QoS (sam.gov, 2026-01, FACT/MEDIUM), and the Army is still funding tooling to model DDIL data delivery (Army SBIR topic, 2025, FACT/HIGH). Anduril opened the Lattice Mesh SDK to third parties (Breaking Defense, 2024-12, FACT/MEDIUM), TAK is a plugin ecosystem with allied reach, and the MVP is unclassified, cheap and open-source-buildable. If a program office or integrator ever wants an engine-agnostic, auditable mission-priority and merge-policy layer - or an impartial DDIL certification harness - a small team that has already built and measured one is the natural partner or acqui-hire (HYPOTHESIS, LOW). This bull case describes a good sub-scale services or tooling business and a possible small exit, not a venture-scale independent company.
